Chapter 9.3

What happens when two or more objects interact?

Motion, turning, shape, pressure and the work a force does

When two or more objects interact, they exert a force on one another. What does that force change?

Learning Objectives

What you will be able to do by the end of this lesson

  • Describe the changes a force can produce in the state of rest or motion of an object.
  • Describe the turning effect of a force about a pivot.
  • Explain how pressure depends on the force applied and the area of contact.
  • Describe pressure in liquids and atmospheric pressure, and where each is applied.
  • State the conditions for work to be done on an object.

Core concept

How does a force change motion?

When two or more objects interact, they exert a force on one another and energy is actually transferred between them!

Learn
  • When two or more objects interact, they exert a force on one another. This results in the transfer of energy between the objects.
  • The transfer of energy between objects may cause changes in the state of rest or motion of an object. It can move a stationary object.
  • It can also change the speed of an object and change the direction in which an object moves.Pedal harder and the bicycle speeds up. Hit a shuttlecock and it goes back the other way. Both are forces changing motion.
  • It can stop a moving object.
Key Facts
  • A force can move a stationary object, change its speed, change its direction, or stop it.
  • Every one of these involves a transfer of energy between the interacting objects.
  • The interaction is always between two or more objects, never one on its own.
Test

A cyclist pedals harder and the bicycle speeds up. Which change has the force produced?

Core concept

What is the turning effect of a force?

Push at a distance from a fixed point and the object turns instead of sliding!

Learn
  • A force applied on an object can cause a turning effect about a fixed point called the pivot.The pivot is the point that stays put. Everything else swings around it, like the hinge of a door.
  • This turning effect can help us to carry out an action with little force, such as removing the lid of a tin can.
  • It also helps us to tighten a nut using a spanner.A long spanner turns a stiff nut that your fingers could never move. The extra length does the work for you.
Key Facts
  • The pivot is the fixed point that the object turns about.
  • The turning effect lets us carry out an action with little force.
  • The force is applied away from the pivot. Applying it at the pivot produces no turning effect.
Test

A student cannot loosen a nut with a short spanner, so she uses a longer one and it moves. Why?

Core concept

What else can a force change?

Some interactions do not move an object at all. They change what it looks like instead!

Learn
  • The transfer of energy between objects may cause changes in the size and/or shape of an object.
  • A balloon changes in size when air is pumped into it.
  • A sponge changes in shape when a force is applied to squeeze it.The sponge is still the same sponge and there is still the same amount of it. Only its shape has changed.
  • A lump of plasticine changes in size and shape when it is cut into smaller pieces.
Key Facts
  • A change in shape does not need the object to move anywhere.
  • Cutting changes both the size and the shape of an object.
  • Every one of these changes involves a transfer of energy between the objects.
Test

A student squeezes a sponge in her hand. Which change has the force produced?

Core concept

Why does a pin go in more easily than a nail?

The same force spread over a SMALLER area produces a HIGHER pressure.

Learn
  • Pressure is an effect of force acting on an object.
  • When we carry a backpack, it exerts a pressure on our shoulders. The amount of pressure depends on whether we carry the backpack using one or two straps, and how much the contents of our backpack weigh.Two straps spread the same load over twice as much shoulder. Each shoulder feels less, even though the bag has not got any lighter.
  • The pin, which has a very small area of contact, exerts a very high pressure on the cork board. Thus, it can be pushed into the cork board easily.
  • The nail has a larger area of contact, so it exerts a lower pressure and is pushed into the cork board with some difficulty.

    • Your mother tells you to carry your backpack using both straps. Explain why using both straps makes the backpack feel more comfortable, using the concept of pressure.

Key Facts
  • Pressure depends on two things: the force applied and the area of contact.
  • The same force on a smaller area gives a higher pressure.
  • Pressure is defined as force per unit area.
Test

A pin and a nail are pushed into a cork board using the same amount of force. Why does the pin go in more easily?

📓Now complete your notes: Section D: What pressure depends onComplete the pin and nail comparison table.
Application

Where do we make use of pressure every day?

Let's explore some real world examples :)

Learn
  • An injection needle needs to be very sharp so that the area of contact of the needle with the skin is very small. When we apply a force on the needle, a high pressure allows the sharp needle to pierce the skin easily.
  • The heel of a high-heeled shoe has a smaller area of contact with a surface than the heel of a sneaker, so it exerts a higher pressure on the surface.All of the person's weight goes through a heel the size of a coin instead of a heel the size of a hand. That small patch takes everything.
  • A sharp knife has a smaller area of contact with a tomato than a blunt knife. With the same amount of force applied, a sharp knife exerts a higher pressure, so it is able to cut the tomato more easily.
Key Facts
  • Pressure is calculated as force divided by area.
  • The unit of pressure is newton per square metre, also known as the pascal (Pa).
  • Sharper means a smaller area of contact, which means a higher pressure for the same force.
Test

A woman in high-heeled shoes and a woman in sneakers have the same weight. Why is the high heel more likely to crack a phone screen?

Core concept

How do engineers design for pressure in liquids?

When you swim to the bottom of the pool, you feel more pressure and your ears starts ringing.

Learn
  • As we move deeper underwater, we feel a higher pressure acting on our body.
  • The base of a dam has a much thicker wall than its top. This is because water pressure is higher at the base of the dam and a thicker wall is better able to withstand the higher pressure.
  • As sea levels rise due to climate change, the water pressure at the seabed increases. Thus, the base of a dam will need to have an even thicker wall.More water above means more pressure below. If the sea gets higher, the wall at the bottom has more to hold back.
  • Submarines dive to great depths underwater. The pressure deep below the water surface can be very high, so a submarine needs a strong body to withstand this high pressure.
Key Facts
  • Water pressure increases as the depth increases.
  • Every submarine has a depth limit, which keeps it at a safe depth where the water pressure is not high enough to damage its physical structure.
  • The blobfish lives at 600 to 1200 metres, where the water pressure is more than 60 times the pressure at the surface of the sea.
Test

Why does a dam wall need to be thicker at its base than at its top?

Core concept

Atmospheric Pressure

If water can apply pressure on us, what about the thousands of kilometers of air above us?

Learn
  • Earth is surrounded by a thick layer of air. Air particles are light, occupy space and have mass.
  • When the layer of air particles pushes down on Earth's surface due to gravitational force, it exerts a pressure of approximately 100 000 Pa at sea level. This pressure is called atmospheric pressure.There is a column of air stretching from your head up to space. It is light, but there is a great deal of it, and it all presses down.
  • When we are at a height above sea level, for example on a mountain, fewer air particles push down on us. Hence, the atmospheric pressure exerted on us decreases.
  • Tropical cyclones can arise due to differences in atmospheric pressure. The sun warms the water on the ocean surface, causing it to evaporate. The warm air rises, creating an area of lower air pressure near the surface of the ocean, and air from the surrounding area of higher air pressure flows into it.Warm air lifts away and leaves a gap near the surface. Air nearby rushes in to fill it, and that rushing air is the wind of a storm.
Key Facts
  • Atmospheric pressure is approximately 100 000 Pa at sea level.
  • Atmospheric pressure decreases as height above sea level increases.
  • Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer.
Test

Why is atmospheric pressure lower on a mountain top than at sea level?

Core concept

When is work done on an object?

In science, work has a much stricter meaning than it does in everyday speech!

Learn
  • In some cases, a force applied causes an object to move in the same direction as the force. This results in a transfer of energy. When energy is transferred, we say that work is done through the application of the force.
  • When no energy is transferred even though a force is applied, we say that no work is done.Push a wall as hard as you like. Nothing moves, so nothing has been transferred, so no work has been done.
  • The transfer of energy and the amount of work done through the application of a force have the same SI unit, which is the joule (J).
  • For work to be done on an object, a force must be applied on the object, the object must move, and the object must move in the same direction as the force applied on it.
Key Facts
  • All three conditions must be met, not just one of them.
  • There may be many forces acting on an object at the same time. Only the force applied in the same direction as the motion will determine whether work is done.
  • Chemical potential energy of the boy is converted to gravitational potential energy of the box as he lifts it.
Test

A boy carries a box across a room at a steady height. Is work done on the box by the force holding it up?
